choices.content: Not necessarily; the angle must be the included angle between the two sides
They are necessarily congruent by SSA

question.prompt: If two triangles have two pairs of equal sides and one pair of equal angles, are they necessarily congruent?

solutions.explanation: SAS requires the equal angles to be the included angles between the two sides. If the angles are opposite one of the sides (SSA), congruence is not guaranteed.
solutions.title: Distinguish SAS from SSA
